title: Basket vines
subtitle: Kouloura
objectives: Explain the threat to Santorini's vineyards

steps.title: Baskets
steps.body: Santorini's vines are trained into kouloura, low baskets woven from the vine's own canes, lying on the ground. The grapes grow inside the basket. Each year, new canes are woven in, so the basket grows. After 50 to 80 years, the basket is cut off, and a new one grows from the same old roots.

steps.title: Why baskets
steps.body: The kouloura protects grapes from strong winds, which can strip leaves and fruit, from fierce sun and from blowing volcanic sand. Inside, the grapes catch moisture from night sea mist and dew, the vines' main water source. The low shape keeps the vines close to the cooler, more humid ground.
steps.highlight: Shelter from wind, sun and sand

steps.prompt: What does the kouloura protect against?
steps.explanation: Santorini has mild winters; frost isn't the main concern.

steps.title: Threats
steps.body: Santorini's vineyards are shrinking. Tourism has made land extremely valuable, and many vineyards have been built on. Low yields, drought and climate change add pressure. Producers like Hatzidakis, Gaia, Sigalas and Santo Wines work to protect the vines and their heritage.

options: A basket-shaped vine trained on the ground
steps.explanation: Woven from the vine's own canes.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Kouloura vines are woven into baskets on the ground
They protect grapes from wind, sun and sand
Tourism and drought threaten Santorini's vineyards
